candidates.exact_span: 4Q3   Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: This defines the design-flow statistic used when permit limits or monitoring conditions are keyed to low-flow or flow-dependent criteria; a different reading of what 4Q3 denotes (duration, averaging window, or recurrence interval) could change which numeric limit applies or whether a flow-conditioned monitoring requirement is in effect.

candidates.exact_span: BOD   Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The parenthetical qualifies which BOD variant the abbreviation denotes; interpreting BOD as five-day versus another test duration would change which enforceable numeric limit is matched to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: ug/L       Micrograms per litter (one part per billion)
candidates.computation_change_reason: This supplies the unit basis for microgram-per-liter reporting; ambiguity in the stated unit (including the spelling 'litter' versus 'liter') could change unit conversion when comparing reported values to limits expressed in other units.

candidates.exact_span: mg/L  Milligrams per liter (one part per million)
candidates.computation_change_reason: This defines the milligram-per-liter reporting basis; a different interpretation of the stated equivalence to parts per million could affect conversion and comparison of reported measurements against applicable numeric limits.

How MQL is understood determines whether a reported or non-reported value can be treated as a numeric result suitable for limit comparison versus a below-quantification or missing-evidence state that should not be scored as an ordinary exceedance or compliance finding.

Reasonable-potential findings can trigger derivation or imposition of more stringent limits and associated monitoring; different interpretation of what RP means in this permit context could change which limits are treated as applicable and which monitoring duties follow.
Critical dilution is used in water-quality-based limit derivation; interpreting CD differently could change the numeric effluent limits deemed applicable to a discharge.

CFU defines the enumeration unit for microbiological results; treating a measurement as CFU-based versus another unit basis would change which numeric limit applies and which microbiological monitoring results are comparable.

This identifies the fecal-coliform parameter family; interpreting whether reported results map to FCB versus another coliform indicator would change the applicable numeric limit and the monitoring parameter being evaluated.

MPN specifies an alternate microbiological enumeration method; classifying results as MPN-based versus CFU-based affects limit matching, which monitoring methodology was required, and how absent or non-numeric microbiological evidence should be categorized.

pH limits are expressed in standard units rather than mass/volume concentrations; misinterpreting s.u. could cause pH measurements to be compared against the wrong numeric limit type or excluded from numeric compliance comparison incorrectly.

DMR defines the evidentiary vehicle for self-monitoring; different interpretation of what counts as DMR-submitted monitoring could change whether a monitoring obligation is treated as required, satisfied, or lacking adequate evidence.
